A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(i) the proU operons of E. coli K-12 and E. coli B/r are virtually identical, (ii) the proV gene encodes a protein with a structure similar to that of other membrane-associated components of binding-protein-dependent permeases, (iii) the ProW protein has structural similarities to the membrane components above and to the periplasmically located glycine betaine transport protein BetP of Corynebacterium glutamicum, (iv)
the proU operonic DNA contains all the structural and regulatory information required for osmotic control of glycine betaine transport in E. coli.

the DNA sequence data, in combination with genetic and biochemical data, have led us to propose a model for glycine betaine uptake in Escherichia coil in which ProX, ProW, and ProV function, respectively, as the binding protein, the membrane-associated permease, and the energy-transducing component of the transport system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we now have a detailed molecular description of the proU locus, which will allow us to address the question of how this locus is controlled at the molecular level.
the proU operons of E. coli and Salmonella typhimurium are remarkably similar in structure and organization.
the proV, proW and proX genes encode the components of a binding-protein-dependent glycine betaine transport system.
